source_span: We interpret this as effectively signaling a hawkish bias, with the intent of keeping December as a live option for the Committee's next hike. We continue to expect a hike at the December FOMC meeting.
source_chain: FOMC added the 'accumulation of more information' sentence therefore JPM reads it as a deliberate hawkish bias meant to keep December live therefore JPM still forecasts a December hike; separately, Warsh's presser gave no clear rationale for the pause therefore (per JPM) the market itself came out less convinced a December plan exists, though JPM's own call is unchanged. No explicit invalidation condition is stated by JPM in this note.
pulse_chain: FOMC upgraded its economic description and added the same new sentence therefore the pulse reports JPM reads it as a deliberate hawkish bias meant to keep December alive therefore JPM still expects a hike then; the press conference pulled the other way, with Warsh giving no clear rationale, therefore the pulse reports (attributed to JPM) that the market came out less convinced of a December plan. The theme's own invalidation (the next day's core PCE print) is framed generally, not attributed to JPM.
why: Both of the pulse's JPM-attributed steps (statement-as-hawkish-bias keeping the December hike call alive, and the presser denting the market's not JPM's conviction) match the note's own sequence and attribution, and the pulse does not put an invalidation into JPM's mouth that JPM didn't argue.
